thread.title: Apple Pares Gains But On Track For Big Week; Bitcoin Below $10K

author: NANCY GONDO
title: Apple Pares Gains But On Track For Big Week; Bitcoin Below $10K
text:
Key market index funds were mixed Friday as Apple ( AAPL ) gave up most of its gains and Bitcoin reversed lower.
X SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ( DIA ) was nearly flat and SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ) rose 0.3%. PowerShares QQQ Trust ( QQQ ) fell 0.2%. DIA and SPY were testing their 50-day moving average lines. QQQ remains 2% above the support line.
Apple was up 0.2% after giving up a 1% gain. It's holding above both the 50-day and 200-day lines, and is on track to extend its win streak to six sessions. Shares are 3% below their January peak. Apple gapped up and advanced more than 3% Thursday to close above the 50-day line. The iPhone maker is on track for a weekly gain of 11%.
Small caps outperformed: iShares Core S&P Small-Cap ( IJR ) and iShares Russell 2000 ( IWM ) were up 0.6% each.
IBD Survey: What New ETFs Would You Like To See Created? 
Metals miners, homebuilders and oil services were among biggest sector fund gainers in the stock market today . But gold miners, consumer discretionary and biotechs lagged.
Bitcoin slipped below the $10K level, down 0.5% to $9.969.46, according to CoinDesk . It had risen to $10,293.44 earlier. Bitcoin Investment Trust ( GBTC ), which continues to hit upward resistance at its 50-day, gave up 4%. IBM on Wednesday warned Congress about blockchain overregulation .
How Now, Dow? The recent market sell-off is creating plenty of new buy opportunities, including a popular ETF that counts Apple and Boeing ( BA ) among its top holdings.
In just two weeks, SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ( DIA ) crashed 12% from its Jan. 26 intraday high to its Feb. 9 session low. But it extended its win streak Thursday to five days and recovered its 50-day moving average . With the market back in a confirmed uptrend, a solid move above the support line sets up a potential buy area.
The ETF advanced 22% from a mid-August bounce off the 50-day to its Jan. 26 peak. It was last featured in this ETF column on Sept. 15. At that time, it was still in buy range from the pullback to the line.
The $22.7 billion behemoth, which celebrated its 19th anniversary last month, tracks the Dow Jones industrial average. The price-weighted index is composed of 30 blue chip U.S. stocks. The top 10 holdings as of Feb. 14 included Boeing, Goldman Sachs ( GS ), Apple, Caterpillar ( CAT ) and Travelers ( TRV ). Together, the top 10 stocks accounted for 56% of total
assets.
Boeing leads the five stocks mentioned above with a 21% gain year to date. Goldman Sachs was up 5% for the year, through Thursday's close. Travelers followed with a 4% return, while Apple and Caterpillar had climbed 2% each.
Apple had a big day Thursday, rising more than 3% to retake its 50-day line. Billionaire investor Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway ( BRKB ) disclosed in a regulatory filing an increased stake in the iPhone maker in Q4.
